feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/communications CV with credible scope, clear public-sector positioning, and solid evidence of progression. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness and impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo from coordinator to director, then consulting, which builds credibility well.  
- Good use of scale indicators: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add impact and specificity.  
- Broad but coherent skill set across strategy, platforms, analytics, governance, and multimedia; well aligned to the headline.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy / governance / workflows / content operations” appears across summary, competencies, skills, and roles. Consolidate to avoid redundancy.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or campaign performance.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “AI-enabled” repeated very often, and mixed punctuation/list style. Minor grammar/style edits: remove comma in “web, email, social, and multimedia” for consistency; “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No obvious misspellings or major typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and sector focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience sections. Tightening it and adding one concrete scale cue would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider a sharper version: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise website transformation, analytics and reporting infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with “modernizing web platforms” for clearer, more active phrasing.
- Use “website transformation” or “web modernization” consistently with the rest of the CV.
- If space allows, add one scale signal from recent work, e.g. “10,000+ page website” or “3.5 million annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it broad here and save specifics for those sections.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely echoes the subtitle and competencies; avoid stacking too many parallel descriptors.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinct will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, sharper labels and keep parallel structure throughout.
- Prioritize the strongest, most marketable themes first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows elsewhere, replace one broad item with a more differentiated strength such as “Drupal platform delivery” or “Cross-functional digital operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” repeats language already used in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” also overlaps with multiple NACo roles and the Topline Skills section.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short intro line like “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent verb style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot” for style consistency.
- Make each project more specific by foregrounding the deliverable or audience impact, e.g., “legislative search,” “Drupal 10 microsite,” “conference installation.”
- Consider this tighter rewrite:  
  **AI Hybrid Search:** Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level chat.  
  **We Are Counties Microsite:** Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources in a scalable modular framework.  
  **Organization Anniversary Campaign:** Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10-by-20-foot interactive conference display.  
  **Advocacy Video Series:** Produced a recurring advocacy video series spanning editorial planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with Work Experience bullets; keep only if this footer is meant as a visual “selected projects” summary.
- “Built/Developed” repeats frequently; vary verbs slightly if space allows.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project footer. Make it more outcome-led and anchor it to 3–4 highest-value contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into impact areas: digital operations/analytics, Drupal campaign builds, governance, and AI search.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing teams enabled, or efficiency gains.
- Tighten phrasing. Example bullets:
- Built Drupal microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits for major campaigns.
- Improved communications workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and discovery UX.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this bullet shorter here.
- Governance/analytics/web improvement also echo the summary and prior NACo role.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/operational leadership, and the most senior-level achievements without repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the website bullet into a sharper outcome line: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make analytics/governance more results-oriented: add adoption, reporting speed, decision-making, or workflow efficiency metrics if available.
- Reframe video studio bullet to show business value: e.g., reduced vendor reliance, increased production volume, or expanded advocacy/event coverage.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; either cut it or add stronger outcomes.
- “Publishing standards and cross-department planning” is close to earlier editorial coordination language; keep this version focused on enterprise governance.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like responsibilities than achievements. Tighten it to emphasize what changed under your leadership and quantify outputs where possible.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + outcome: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging organization-wide.”
- Combine newsletter/video bullets and add metrics if available: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching [X]+ county officials and stakeholders, and produced a weekly advocacy video series that established video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Make cross-functional impact more active: “Built tighter editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving alignment and publishing cadence.”
- Replace “helped improve” with a stronger result: “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with both the earlier Digital Media Manager role and the Recent Projects section.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” also appears in the Director of Digital Media entry; differentiate this role as execution/scale-up rather than governance leadership.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • dashboard development • SEO analysis • experimentation”

- This item substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one version or making this one tools-only and the topline version outcomes/capabilities-only.
- “SEO” also overlaps with broader digital strategy language elsewhere; keep it only if it’s a genuine hands-on strength.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can add metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten phrasing and separate scope from outcomes: “Improved workflows across web, email, social and multimedia; supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Add measurable detail where possible: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social support volume, or size/timing of the website refresh.
- Clarify supervision modestly: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate on daily production and publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on launching/producing the series, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating governance/strategy language already covered more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Replace generic phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer scope and support function.
- Split into 2 concise bullets; emphasize ownership verbs: launched, managed, supported, produced.
- If possible, add outcomes: number of episodes, audience/listens, internal stakeholders supported, or types of policy/program outputs.

Suggested edit
- Supported county innovation and research initiatives that informed NACo programmatic and policy work.
- Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, planning, scripting, recording coordination and production; also produced digital and multimedia content supporting organizational communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on the podcast launch and innovation/research support.
- Avoid broad claims about digital leadership here since stronger, more recent evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tighten it to emphasize current, professional production tools and avoid repeating broader multimedia themes already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/reshape for consistency: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production • Podcast production”
- Replace “Livestream studio workflows” with a cleaner noun phrase like “Livestream production” or “Studio production workflows.”
- If true, add one higher-value tool or system tied to recent work (e.g., “PTZ camera systems” or streaming platforms), rather than generic creative apps.
- Keep this item tool-focused; let work experience carry the impact. If possible, align wording with recent studio/video leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream” and “Podcast production” overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills; this section should stay as a concise tools/platforms list.
- Photoshop/Illustrator may feel secondary unless regularly used in recent roles; consider dropping one if space is tight.
